The industry row stays C because the industry is split: Semiconductors (D), Software B2B Enterprise (D), Fintech (D) and Games (D) carry the Underweight; IT services, Hardware and vertical software stay Neutral. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: A now, A prior, the disagreement stated: the market still ranks the sector first while cutting its multiple. Ten of the 149 Pool stocks. Counter-case: the analogue upcycle 'has more legs' into 2027, demand was never the problem, and a D on ten Pool names pushes the Lists away from the one European industry with upgrades; the analogue read is a reason to look at STMicroelectronics stock by stock, not to move a row that is mostly equipment.

memo.verdict: Neutral; park, for valuation. Infineon (IFX-DE) at €59.42 (2026-10-01) is a 'Demand Inflection' case whose operations are compelling and fully evidenced down the 'Six Layer Inputs-outputs' chain, at a price that already pays for consensus delivery and a modest re-rating. The 'Modal return' on our modal path, valued at 16.3x (the stock's ten-year median 24-month-forward multiple) the earnings two years beyond each horizon, is 1.7% a year over eighteen months (2028-04-01; value including cash returns €60.95) and 4.5% a year over three years (2029-10-01; €67.76), against the framework's 20% bar: an F. The consensus path at the same multiple gives about 20% a year, which is what the price assumes. Two re-entry triggers: a price below about €46 (the eighteen-month bar on our path at the median multiple; about €42 on the adverse drop-through ratio), or evidence at the 10-Nov-26 results that growth beyond FY2028 is above our 10% a year (a FY2027 AI target well above €3bn with a raised 2030 addressable-market framework, or Dresden utilisation disclosure implying more than €2bn of revenue by FY2028). Conviction medium on the operations (the chain is fully evidenced) and medium on the price (the summer's fall of a third is unexplained by our files and cuts both ways). The park rule is not triggered: management B, business quality B, predictability A, trackability C. The record is a Triaging-stage experiment prototype dated 2026-10-02, by Chris the Investment Analyst, evidence convention A.
case: - The external change is a demand explosion written into contracts. Dedicated AI data-centre power revenue €250m FY2024, over €700m FY2025, over €1.6bn guided FY2026; FY2027 target €2.5bn, a floor, to be raised 10-Nov-26. Capacity reservation agreements with more than ten hyper-scalers and AI chipmakers cover high-single-digit billions of euros with prepayments and volume-shortfall penalties, so visibility exceeds two years and part of the demand risk and capital cost has moved to the customer. The server power component addressable market is projected +60% to 70% a year in 2026 and 2027; rack power moves from 50kW to 100kW to 600kW today and 1MW by 2030; content $175 per kW towards $250. Infineon holds over 40% of AI data-centre power against Renesas at 10% to 12%. Demand (KQ 1, RA 1, E 1, BB 1) A.

- The company's own cycle has turned: quarterly revenue troughed at €3,424m in Q1 FY2025 and rose six consecutive quarters to €4,172m (year-on-year -7.5%, -1.1%, +0.1%, +0.6%, +7.0%, +6.2%, +12.6%); Q4 guided about €4.7bn, +13% sequential; prior peak €4,149m in Q4 FY2023 at 25.2% margin, now exceeded on revenue not margin. Tier-1 order entry picked up, Chinese OEM programme activity +8% to 9%, distributor inventories cleared at the 10- to 12-week target, lead times extending, cancellations falling, customers paying expedite fees. Cycle A.

- The external headwinds are real but sized or being exited: Chinese share of China's automotive power-module market 52% (2022) to 76% (2025); low-end silicon IGBT prices -10% to -15% on SMIC and Hua Hong overcapacity; Texas Instruments 20% to 50% discounts in general-purpose analog; contractual automotive price declines 4% to 7% a year, high-voltage modules -10% to -15%; EUR/USD 1.11 FY2025 to 1.17 H1 FY2026, about €400m of FY2026 revenue, a 1-cent move about €100m of annual revenue and €40m of Segment Result, a 10% dollar fall de-rating EPS over 12% on a three-month hedge (STMicroelectronics hedges 24 months); precious metals, energy (exposure €200m to over €500m), logistics and 300mm wafers (+10% to 20%) capping the Q4 guide; EV subsidy withdrawals in Germany, France and the US; light-vehicle production about 91m units, -1% to -2%; China 25% domestic-content guidance; a Supreme People's Court injunction on specific GaN products with RMB 10m damages. Offsets: SiC substrate deflation (more than six qualified suppliers, Chinese vendors about 20% of requirements); Chips Act €1bn (20% of the Dresden outlay); ESMC $10bn facility with €5bn state aid from late 2027; automotive content +12% to 15% a year; the automotive segment +11% excluding the high-voltage restructuring despite flat units. External forces B; competition C; macro C; supply B; disruption B (800V DC, vertical power delivery, first 300mm GaN, zonal SDV with over 55% of new automotive procurement; against it only the integrated-voltage-regulator risk after 2028, classed as opinion); political C; hedging asymmetry C.
counter_case: - At Building Block 1, the sell-side's structural-breakout case at full force: capacity reservation agreements with more than ten hyper-scalers and AI chipmakers covering high-single-digit billions of euros with prepayments and shortfall penalties; a Dresden fab adding over €2bn of revenue capacity in two to three years and up to €5bn at maturity; a CPU-inference second engine (CPU power addressable market $1.2bn in 2025 to $6.0bn by 2030, Bernstein's sizing); Bernstein's FY2028 AI revenue of €4.5bn and a Segment Result Margin near 30%; a 42% EPS compound rate through FY2028; targets of €96 to €124; the third-lowest multiple in its sector with the sector's best momentum. On that path FY2028 EPS is €4.5 to €5.5, the 24-month-forward figure at eighteen months above €5, and even at 16.3x the eighteen-month value is above €82, a 25% a year return. We concede the AI line could be about €1bn above our FY2028 figure (about €0.25 of EPS at a 40% segment margin, 22% tax, 1,308m shares) and a 27% peak-cycle margin is possible (about €0.27); together they take our FY2028 EPS to about €3.80, the consensus mean, and the eighteen-month return at 16.3x to about 10% a year, from F to D, not to B. We hold because the price's assumption is the compounding after FY2028, and management's own framework (€8bn to €12bn at 30% to 40% by 2030, €2.4bn to €4.8bn) places the AI line in FY2028 where the sell-side has it; the inflection is front-loaded and then grows at the market, so rolling 24-month-forward earnings decelerate sharply from April 2028; the stock's own history says the multiple falls with the sector regardless of delivery. Where it would win: a raised 2030 framework in November, or Dresden utilisation implying more than €2bn by FY2028.

- At Building Block 2, the risks report's false-friend profile: AI power at a 55% to 60% gross margin, pruned high-voltage revenue optically lifting automotive margins, and an October 2024 reclassification of production expenses to R&D together mask terminal share loss in Chinese power and structural underutilisation; the tells are adjusted net income 78% above reported (€1,809m against €1,014m FY2025), €11.1bn of intangibles with goodwill the auditor's key audit matter, and 175 to 183 days of inventory. We concede the accounting gap and that automotive margin at 18.4% is far from 25% with China pricing the cause. We do not concede the mask: the AI line is reported separately and growing over 100% a year; the high-voltage exit is 7% of automotive revenue and was announced; the automotive segment grew 11% excluding it; the report's own two profile inconsistencies (the €650m idle-cost penalty; the 18.1% automotive margin) are now moving the right way (idle costs about €150m a quarter; automotive +5.6% sequential). The risk is real at the margin line, which is why margin is held at the target and 18% is an Alarm level.
triggers: - Why the shares fell a third from the late-July peak with rising estimates; the first question for the 10-Nov-26 print; the research explains only the 6% after 5 and 6-Aug-26.

- The November results: the FY2027 AI target (market expects over €2.8bn; Alarm below €2.8bn; Invalidate below €2.3bn; re-entry evidence well above €3bn with a raised 2030 framework); first FY2027 guidance (needs to clear about €19.9bn of revenue for the next leg of revisions); first Dresden utilisation disclosure (re-entry evidence: more than €2bn of revenue by FY2028); Q4 FY2026 Segment Result Margin (confirm at or above 23%; Alarm below 22%; a print at or above 24% with Power Systems at 30% or more would say the mix is already doing the work and move us towards consensus's 27%); the Q4 FX assumption of 1.15 against 1.17 recent; whether the industrial segment rebounds sharply in Q4 as promised.

- Price triggers: re-enter below about €46 (eighteen-month bar on our path), about €42 on the adverse drop-through, about €39 for both horizons. The multiple: Alarm below 13.96x without an estimate cut; Invalidate below 11.9x; evidence that the summer's fall was company-specific (a cut) moves us to the uncleared branch; a print clearing delivery and sector recovery together moves us to 19.2x.

- Growth beyond FY2028 (likely to fall to 8% to 10%, about 60%): changed by a raised addressable-market framework or Dresden disclosure implying more than €2bn by FY2028. The FY2028 margin (probable 24% in FY2027 and 25% to 26% in FY2028, about 65%; consensus's 27% possible, about 35%).

- The automotive and industrial cycle holding through FY2027 (probable, about 65%): backlog below €25bn Alarm, below €22bn Invalidate; automotive margin below 18% Alarm, below 16% for two quarters Invalidate.

- Hyper-scaler capacity agreements: one scaled back Alarm; three or more Invalidate (also the review's trigger). Idle costs above €200m a quarter Alarm, above €800m a year Invalidate. Inventory days above 180 Alarm. EUR/USD above 1.20 Alarm, above 1.25 Invalidate. Chinese entrants' 8-inch SiC fabs replicating IGBT deflation in SiC and MOSFETs by FY2027; Chinese quality reaching automotive grade within 24 months.
